x: The handicap held in conjunction, was won by Doub off a generous 6m.10s. with Syd James 2nd and Eric Hall 3rd., the latter two being off scratch.
Could Eric and Syd continue their good form, and what of George Beecham, Maurice Nye, Bill True and Doub, who was going to make up the team.
Norman Milsum had just held of Doub to be the first of our "B" Team. Bert East and Logan had a dust up for 173rd position followed by our second claim member Tubby Gittins.
By my reckoning Charlie Speechley must be over 60, Charlie Jones over 40, Tom Carter almost 95, Doub getting on for 35 but none looked any older than when I joined the Club in 1948.
Having said all that, my thanks once again, and I look forward to the next issue from my "Home Counties" venue (not so Doub. this part of Essex is definitely East Anglia!)

"Doub" could be relied on to know what was required and then to deliver the placing - on occasion due to the absence of our stars. His spell as Hon Treasurer, from 1950 to 1952, was after a wartime move to Exeter where he became involved with the local club.
